subject: Step-change threshold language — order schedule redline and packaging mapping
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novushealth.com>, Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Step-change threshold language — order schedule redline and packaging mapping

Hi Jenna / Novus procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — attaching a cleaned-up redline of the Order Schedule that captures the pricing guardrails we discussed. The two items we want to make sure are explicit are: (1) an approach to the step-change thresholds that avoids a hard "cliff" pricing jump, and (2) clear packaging mapping so SKU bundling doesn't unintentionally trigger higher tiers.

Quick summary of the edits in RDF_OrderSchedule_v3_redline.pdf (attached):
- Section 2.3 (Thresholds): replaced hard step with a 30-day smoothing window and a true-up mechanism to reconcile actual usage over the smoothing window.
- Section 2.3.2 (Clawback): limited clawback exposure to 60 days and capped at the incremental delta between tiers.
- Section 4 (Packaging & SKU mapping): added a mapping table example and an ops-runbook requirement for how Novus will file SKU bundle definitions to avoid misclassification.

Action items for Novus: please confirm whether legal will accept the smoothing-window + true-up approach or if they prefer a different mitigation (e.g., proration per invoice cycle). Also call out any procurement constraints around minimum notice for true-ups.

I know your counsel was concerned about open‑ended true-ups — the attached workbook (pricing-elevator-workbook.xlsx) models both the soft-step and an alternate proration approach so you can see dollar impact.

If helpful I can loop Laura and our pricing ops (Kimberly) into a short call early next week to walk the redline.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: RDF_OrderSchedule_v3_redline.pdf, pricing-elevator-workbook.xlsx

From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Step-change threshold language — order schedule redline and packaging mapping

Rafael —

Appreciate the note and the files. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the PDF and have inline comments (attached as Novus_Redline_comments.pdf). High-level feedback:  

- We are sympathetic to a "soft-step" but Novus counsel is worried that a smoothing window combined with a capped clawback still creates an unpredictable liability. They asked whether we can limit exposure to a single quarterly reconciliation rather than a rolling true-up.
- Packaging mapping: procurement agrees there needs to be a canonical mapping, but operations asked for a two-week notice requirement for any bundle changes that could affect tiering — otherwise we risk mid‑cycle reclassifications.
- Tier anchors: legal wants a floor protection for the first 90 days after go-live (to account for baseline instability).

We proposed two edits in our redline: replace the 30-day smoothing window language with a quarterly true-up (calendar quarter) and add a 90-day post-go-live floor exception. Please see Novus_Redline_comments.pdf for the exact markup.

Can you send back a version that shows a quarterly true-up option? Also you mentioned a workbook — would you share a worked example that shows the difference between: 1) 30-day smoothing + monthly true-up, 2) quarterly reconciliation, and 3) invoice-level proration.

Happy to set a call Wed 10–11am PT if you and your team are available.

Thanks,
Jenna Ortiz
Senior Director, Procurement | Novus Health
jenna.ortiz@novushealth.com | (617) 555-8821

Attachments: Novus_Redline_comments.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Step-change threshold language — order schedule redline and packaging mapping

Team — forwarding Novus' redline and ask. They want to replace the 30-day smoothing window with a quarterly reconciliation and add a 90-day post-go-live floor. Legal flagged predictability risk of the clawback even when capped.

Short questions for ops/legal/pricing:
- Laura: is a quarterly true-up materially worse than the 30‑day smoothing from a legal risk perspective? They want a single reconciliation per quarter vs rolling adjustments.
- Kimberly: from a pricing ops and billing standpoint, what burden does a quarterly reconciliation + floor exception introduce? Can we implement the "two-week notice for bundle changes" that Novus wants without adding manual work?
- Karthik: any commercial appetite to accept a 90‑day floor post-go-live? We could offer a time-limited carve (90d) in exchange for a modestly higher initial commit (e.g., 5% uplift on year 1 commit) — would that help the deal economics?

Attached: Novus_Redline_comments.pdf and our previous RDF_OrderSchedule_v3_redline.pdf and the pricing workbook (pricing-elevator-workbook.xlsx).

If you prefer, let's take the Wed 10am PT slot and walk the scenarios live before returning an updated order schedule. Jenna, will you confirm the Wed slot?

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Step-change threshold language — order schedule redline and packaging mapping

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. I reviewed Novus' comments and drafted two short alternatives we can offer back:

Option A (Commercially neutral, operations-friendly):
- Keep smoothing window but change to a 45-day smoothing window (compromise between 30 and quarterly).
- Cap clawback exposure at 60 days of incremental delta and limit total dollar exposure to a percentage of the quarterly commit (e.g., max 15% of quarter commit).
- Accept Novus' two-week notice for bundle mappings but require that Novus provide an ops contact and a single canonical file (CSV) for bundle definitions; any changes to the file take effect at the next billing cycle after receipt.

Option B (Concession to procurement/legal):
- Accept a single quarterly true-up (calendar quarter).
- Add a 90-day post-go-live floor protection.
- In exchange, require: (i) a modest one-time onboarding fee (waived if Novus meets year-1 commit), and (ii) a 5% uplift to year-1 committed spend for the floor concession.

Both options include a mutual audit right limited to once per year and a dispute escalation path to a named ops lead before any clawback billing is applied.

If you all agree, I can convert Option A and Option B into two short redlined paragraphs for insertion into Section 2.3 of the Order Schedule and return to Novus ahead of the Wed call. My recommendation: offer Option A as the primary and keep Option B as a fallback negotiation that buys predictability for Novus.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
